title: CI: adopt DEV-PIPELINE-1 normal development stages and failure handoff
body:
## Outcome

Adopt [AW DEV-PIPELINE-1](https://github.com/faberline/aw/blob/a511a9b08808d973b3c5a76f5e22815992fffa3f/docs/standards/development-pipeline.md) for **normal development PRs** in faberline/lumen. The four-stage/local-review design came from faberline/aw#141. Its CI-success `done` label clarification was merged in faberline/aw#142 at `a511a9b08808d973b3c5a76f5e22815992fffa3f`. Its shared implementation and executable conformance are tracked by faberline/aw#129.

This is a repository-specific workflow/policy adoption issue. It does not authorize release/RC changes, schedule changes, cloud changes, weaker tests, or taking another agent's work.

## Existing work

Coordinate with #184 and PR #187 (qualification framework), and their existing owner. This issue adds the common stage and every-job failure contract; it does not replace their bounded acceptance or claim product gaps are fixed.

Keep both unit/static and the existing GKE functional/E2E/performance acceptance. Preserve HTTP/2, index-latency, pagination and all other original numeric thresholds. Existing missing/zero-test content goes to the issue planner.

## Required implementation

1. **Preflight:** app-defined jobs check a frozen PR/main snapshot for behind-main, merge conflicts, and exactly one valid canonical open issue. Confirmed behind/conflict is a failed job and returns the issue to todo. No/ambiguous link blocks on the PR; never guess an issue.
2. **Impact/test plan:** derive complete changed paths, including deletions and both rename paths, affected dependency users, issue acceptance, required targets/features and expected nonzero test rosters. Pin the reviewed selection policy and frozen commits. Preserve existing broader required gates; missing mappings or content cannot silently select no tests.
3. **Unit/static:** execute every selected unit and applicable format, Clippy, compile/documentation gate. Verify actual roster names/counts. Matrix jobs are allowed; zero tests and unexpected skips cannot pass.
4. **Integration/functional/E2E and performance:** start only after stage 3 succeeds. Use separate logical groups and isolated resources; preserve all existing workloads and thresholds.
### Local review and completion, outside CI

- Start independent Claude Code review locally only after all necessary current-input CI succeeds. Bind the decision to the exact PR, base, issue contract, plan and run attempts. Keep review read-only and execute no candidate programs with review credentials.
- Remove cloud review, merge and issue-close workflows/producer configuration. Retain the CI success label handoff. CI ends after stage 4. Keep one CI label writer with issue-comment/todo/done permission and no contents, PR or status write permission.
- Set `completion_owner: "local"`. Keep full test qualification available to the local reviewer. After all necessary current-input CI succeeds, add the literal `done` label and remove conflicting `todo`/`doing` labels. Keep the issue OPEN for local `issue-review`; CI merges/closes nothing. Missing, skipped, cancelled, stale or failed necessary checks cannot produce `done`.
- Replace the retired cloud `claude/verified-merge` branch requirement with all actual necessary test checks and strict base when the verified local path is ready. Do not remove test requirements or use provider bypass.
- The authorized local controller rechecks all evidence, confirms the exact merge, then closes only the canonical issue. Unknown results reconcile first; retry closure only after a confirmed merge. A rejected/tool-failed local review records its reasons and safely returns only the current attempt to todo.

### Every failed CI job in stages 1–4

- Retain each failed expanded job's step, concise observed reason, category, required/actual result, run/job links, repository/PR/issue/head/base, run attempt and matrix identity.
- Post a human-readable comment with that reason and evidence on the canonical issue, then return the current work attempt to todo. Include setup, checkout, dependency, provisioning, timeout, infrastructure failures.
- Report failures even if downstream jobs are skipped or the failed runner cannot upload a receipt.
- Use the existing single trusted result writer. Different failed matrix jobs each retain a distinct reason; duplicate events must not repeat a comment or handoff.
- If an agent already claimed returned todo, later failures from the old attempt add context without undoing the new doing state or lease. Stale-head failures cannot reset a newer submission.
- Recover partial comment/label writes and unknown completion outcomes. Keep unrelated labels and preserve all active owners and worktrees.
- Local completion is outside CI. A confirmed merged delivery never returns to todo; keep local close-only recovery evidence.

## Acceptance

- Provide executable evidence for all eight conformance groups in DEV-PIPELINE-1, including real stage dependencies and failure-injection controls for **each** CI stage and expanded job.
- Demonstrate per-job issue comments and correct todo handoff; duplicate/multiple failures, stale inputs, active-owner protection and partial write recovery must not lose diagnostics or reassign new work.
- Bind the final reviewed immutable AW implementation revision and actual producer/workflow identities. A standard document or green writer job does not activate this pipeline.
- Preserve all applicable existing tests, thresholds, exact head/base evidence, required checks and strict branch protection. Protected policy/workflow changes require exact-input local independent review and complete coverage-retention evidence. Do not invoke the retired cloud review/publisher grant path.
- The implementation PR itself must pass its complete applicable CI and local independent Claude review before authorized local merge and canonical issue closure.
- Record exact commits, plan, expanded job results, review, actual merge and actual issue closure. Leave unverified portions as pending.
- Missing product tests are separate bounded planner work. Never waive them in this issue.

## Scope and rollout

Scope: this repository's normal-development workflows, test-plan adapters, reviewed qualification policy, failure-writer integration and local review handoff, related controls and operations documentation. Product behavior fixes and release pipeline design are excluded.

Dependency: faberline/aw#129 must publish the verified shared implementation first.
Rollout order: adopt after https://github.com/faberline/core/issues/84; prepare independent work without activating out of order.

AW is the standards/shared-framework repository and has **no Claude-review gate**. Do not apply this product gate to AW.
